scope: Synthetic intent/entity/1-2 hop retrieval. Both strategies share the same deterministic intent classification and entity extraction. This is not universal database superiority.

compile_cost.note: Build cost is paid per derived field generation and must be amortized over reads; high-churn workloads may favor online SQL.

supported: For this repeated semantic intent/entity/graph workload, moving deterministic 1-2 hop relation resolution from query-time SQL joins into an epoch-bound compiled access field preserves 100% Top-1 and materially lowers hot-read latency.
Alias-only text does not remove the compiled-field advantage once the same entity identity is available to both strategies.
not_supported: Faster than a trivial exact-key B-tree lookup; separate current evidence shows plain SQLite wins that class.
Universal superiority over every relational/vector/graph/search database.
Real Clay/Frank OOD answer-quality improvement or target-host equivalence.

architecture_consequence: Use adaptive V14 routing: ordinary indexed lookup for trivial resolved keys; verified semantic sufficiency fields for stable semantic families; compiled intent/entity/graph fields or compositional Pareto frontiers for repeated multi-hop queries; fail-closed entity-resolved graph/NL fallback for misses.
next_falsifiers: real current Clay graph intent/entity families
